20/S0.subgoal: Describe the abstract concept of the Virtual World Generator and its initial required components.

20/S1.subgoal: Explain why physics support is a required component of the virtual world generator.

20/S2.subgoal: Describe how physics support handles complex movement and interactions like collisions.

20/S3.subgoal: Outline the environmental and sensory physics support required for realistic virtual worlds.

20/S4.subgoal: Explain the requirements for a networked collaborative virtual reality experience.

20/S5.subgoal: Describe the process and minimum requirements for building a VWG from scratch using an SDK.

20/S6.subgoal: Compare the advantages and disadvantages of customizing a VWG implementation.

20/S7.subgoal: Evaluate the pros and cons of using a ready-made virtual world generator.

20/S8.subgoal: Review the fundamental questions regarding VR software components and developer choices.

20/S9.subgoal: Define a game engine and describe its function as a middleware for building XR applications.

20/S10.subgoal: Explain the function and layered architecture of a rendering engine.

20/S11.subgoal: Describe the functions of audio and physics engines within a game engine.

20/S12.subgoal: Compare various game engines based on their features and market adoption.

20/S13.subgoal: Differentiate between native and web application deployment strategies.

20/S14.subgoal: Classify and provide examples of tools used for web deployment.

20/S15.subgoal: Summarize the key concepts discussed in the lecture regarding VR software development.
